title: Scientists Revived a Worm Frozen for 46,000 Years

scenes.text: Scientists revived a worm that was frozen for 46,000 years.
It was buried 130 feet down in Siberian permafrost, in an old gopher burrow.
Researchers thawed it in a lab. It crawled out and started reproducing.
Its trick is called cryptobiosis. It stops eating and its metabolism shuts down.
The old record was about 25 years. Some experts question the exact age, but the plants around it dated to 46,000 years.
Frozen for 46,000 years, and then it moved.

description:
Scientists say they revived a roundworm that spent about 46,000 years frozen in Siberian permafrost.
It entered a dormant state called cryptobiosis, and after thawing it moved and started reproducing. The age comes from radiocarbon dating of plant matter around it, though some scientists question it.
Would you thaw something like this in your lab?

first_comment: Its natural lifespan is only one to two months. Which would you rather be: a worm that lives two months, or one that sleeps 46,000 years?
